predecessors.name: Western Satraps
predecessors.text: the Aulikara core where Cliopatria draws the Western Satraps (to 409: 207-214 of 235 cells)

successors.name: Kalachuris of Mahishmati
successors.text: the Kingdom of Malava: Malwa, held under Prakashadharma and Yashodharman

ledger.x: c. 350: the Aulikara house is established at Dashapura. Infobox span "350-545", with the label "350-375" beside "House of Aulikara established" (the extract could not tell which date goes with which label). The page gives no origin date; Drumavardhana, the earliest known member of the second dynasty, is "c. 5th…

c. 515: Prakashadharma defeats the Hun king Toramana and Malwa is held by the Aulikaras. "Prakashadharma defeated the Huna ruler Toramana"; his Risthal inscription is "fl. 515-516 CE" and Yashodharman's reign is given as 515-545. The page gives no date for the defeat; 515 is the inscription and…

c. 545: the Aulikara rule ends. Infobox span to 545 ("Death of Yashodharman 515-545"); "Probably the rule of the Aulikaras ended with Yashodharma"; the Yashodharman page: "his short-lived empire would ultimately disintegrate between c. 530-540 AD". Malwa then fell to the Kalachuris of Mahishmati (undated).

wars.name: Prakashadharma's war against Toramana
wars.outcome: Prakashadharma defeated the Hun ruler Toramana and held Malwa.

wars.name: Yashodharman's defeat of Mihirakula
wars.outcome: Yashodharman "defeated a Huna army and their ruler Mihirakula in 528 AD and drove them out of India".

certainty.note: No border is given; the Aulikara state is named by Dashapura/Mandsaur and Malwa only, and Yashodharman's claimed empire (Brahmaputra to the Western Ocean) is a panegyric, not a frontier.
